items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.lawCode: Amd §66-j, Pub Serv L; amd §1020-g, Pub Auth L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4283

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public service law and the public authorities law,
in relation to the net energy metering for micro-combined heat and
power generating systems


 PURPOSE :
This legislation would expand New York's net metering law by adding
residential Micro-CHP systems to the list of currently eligible
technologies that can be net metered.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Subdivision 1 of §66-j of the Public Service Law is amended to provide
that residential Micro-CHP systems may be eligible for net metering
under certain circumstances.

A new subdivision 1(f) is added to §66-j of the public service law
that defines Micro-CHP systems.

The bill also amends §66-j of the Public Service Law and subdivision
(h) of §1020-g of the Public Authorities Law to require electric
corporations to permit net energy metering for Micro-CHP generating
equipment, and to provide for the interconnection to the electric
system of Micro-CHP generating equipment in the same manner as other
technologies.  Unlike other systems which are subject to net metering,
however, in the event a Micro-CHP customer-generator produces more
electricity than they can use during a billing period, the customer
will be credited for any excess only at the corporation's avoided
costs.

 EXISTING LAW :
Current law permits net energy metering for residential solar, farm
waste, non-residential solar, and residential and/or farm service wind
electric generating systems.

 JUSTIFICATION :
New York State and its residents face significant energy and climate
change challenges. Energy efficiency continues to be the most
cost-effective, and the most immediate way to reduce the burden of
rising energy and environmental costs as well as our energy-related
carbon footprint. The Micro-CHP technology is at the forefront of
energy efficiency. It is essentially a small scale cogeneration device
providing both heat and electricity with the same amount of fuel
needed to operate a standard furnace.  Proliferation of these devices
bring about benefits not only to the homeowner, but also to utility
corporations and society as a whole.  Consider the benefits:

Energy efficiency - typical central power generation delivers only
30-35% of fuel energy; 55-65% is lost as waste heat and the remainder
is lost as a normal function of transmission and distribution losses.
In contrast, a Micro-CHP unit utilizes over 90% of the fuel for fuel
energy. This will result in a 36% reduction in fuel consumption.
Looked at from a macroperspective, the US Department of Energy
estimates that if 20% of US energy needs were met by CHP it would be
the equivalent of taking 154 million cars off of US roads.

Reduced greenhouse gas emissions - lowers the carbon footprint as
follows:

* 86% reduction in NOx;
* 100% reduction in S02; and
* 46% reduction in C02.


Furthermore, Micro-CHP has been identified by the US Environmental
Protection Agency as one of just two technologies to achieve a
"Climate Choice" rating under the Energy Star Program. Climate Choice
is a new partnership program that recognizes emerging technologies
that have the potential to substantially reduce greenhouse gas
emissions once they are more widely adopted.

Grid enhancement - Distributed generation enhances grid reliability
and supports the grid in peak demand times through demand response.

Economic Stimulus - Micro-CHP systems are built right here in New York
State. The US Department of Energy estimates that if 20% of US energy
needs were met by CHP by 2030 it would generate $2348 in new
investment and would create one million new highly skilled jobs. With
cutting-edge technology all ready underway here, New York could be at
the forefront of the benefits arising from this technology.

In sum, using a more efficient process to supply both heat and power
to homes promotes energy efficiency and creates a path toward energy
independence as we increase our nation's energy security. By
essentially doubling the benefits received from each unit of fuel
used, residential energy consumers will now be able to achieve
significantly improved energy efficiency, reduce their energy costs
and reduce pollutant emissions all at the same time. Micro-CHP systems
can achieve most of the environmental benefits of renewable energy
systems at a fraction of the cost.

The bill is necessary to encourage investments in Micro-CHP systems.
These systems will provide significant benefits to residential
consumers such as reduced energy costs and will help the state achieve
its goal of reduced emissions as well. Additionally, the bill will
help achieve the broad state policies of the Public Service
Commission's Energy Efficiency Portfolio Standard program and
NYSERDA's energy efficiency programs. Finally, as these units are
manufactured in New York State, the expanded usage will encourage
economic investment in skilled New York jobs.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill shall take effect immediately.
